data_policy.emitted: names, offsets, counts, strides and digests only

chain.qwc: the low u16 of the tag's low word
chain.tag_id: bits 28..30 of the tag's low word
chain.unit: 128-bit DMA tag qword: 64-bit tag then two 32-bit VIF codes
chain.unpack_decode: cmd>=0x60; vn=(cmd>>2)&3, vl=cmd&3, NUM=byte 2 (0 means 256), the low 10 bits of IMM are the VU address

format.derived_from: the retail disc, not from the Xbox catalogue
differences_from_xbox: the Xbox shape record is 0x100 bytes and the PS2 record is 0x70
PS2 has no vertex_count field; the count is the VIF UNPACK NUM
PS2 has no vertex stream table, no stream strides and no stream pointers
PS2 has no submesh table and no NV2A push buffer; primitives are assembled by a VU1 microprogram invoked with MSCAL
the Xbox position lane is a contiguous FLOAT3 run of stride 12; the PS2 lane is strided FLOAT4, 12 editable bytes every 16
PS2 carries colour (V4_5) and UV (V2_16) lanes inline in the same DMA chain rather than in separate vertex streams

scope: One target is one geometry batch of one stadium SCNE shape: the single multi-vertex VIF UNPACK V4_32 lane inside that batch's DMA chain. Vertex counts, every other UNPACK, every DMA tag and the VU1 microprogram invocation are outside the editable boundary.

eligibility.reason: the batch's DMA chain terminates cleanly with only known VIF codes and every position the lane decodes lies inside the shape's declared bounding sphere

target_common.payload_span_sharing: several batch descriptors may point at the same DMA chain, so one lane can be reachable under more than one target_id; payload_span_target_count says how many, and the writer refuses a recipe that edits two aliases of one lane

topology.writer_policy: preserve every chain byte outside the position payload, including all NUM fields

title: ESPN NFL 2K5 (PS2) stadium position-lane targets
